weekend_summary: Max Verstappen dominated the Singapore weekend in very different conditions: SQ pole (1:31.156), victory in a rain-hit Sprint, Grand Prix pole (1:31.373) and dry Grand Prix victory ahead of Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli. The Sprint began on intermediates after a rain delay, with Russell crashing early and a late Norris/Piastri collision. The dry Grand Prix offers the usable race-pace signal. Mercedes compared specifications: Russell reverted to Baku-spec while Antonelli kept much of the Sepang package; the new front-wing experiment needs rollout-specific caution.

SQ.summary: Verstappen pole in 1:31.156 over Russell (+0.120s), Leclerc P3, Piastri P4, Norris P5.

key_moments.text: Verstappen took Sprint pole by 0.120s over Russell.
Russell was running the older Baku-spec Mercedes; Antonelli was seventh.

S.summary: In wet/drying conditions on intermediate tyres, Verstappen won ahead of Hamilton and Leclerc.

key_moments.text: Start was rain delayed and all drivers began on intermediates.
Russell passed Verstappen initially, then crashed on the opening lap.
Norris and Piastri collided late while battling in drying conditions; Hamilton finished second, Leclerc third.

Q.summary: Verstappen secured GP pole in 1:31.373, Leclerc second just 0.054s back, Hamilton third, Antonelli fourth and Norris fifth.

key_moments.text: Verstappen took pole by 0.054s over Leclerc.
Hadjar could not set a representative time owing to reliability issues.
Russell qualified sixth before serving a power-unit grid penalty.

R.summary: Verstappen controlled a hot/humid, dry Grand Prix from pole and finished 7.335s ahead of Leclerc; Antonelli took third.

key_moments.text: Verstappen defended the lead at Turn 1 and retained control on soft-to-medium tyres.
Leclerc finished P2 and Antonelli P3; McLaren finished P4/P5.
Russell recovered to P9 after grid penalties, while Hadjar finished P10 from the pit lane.

VER.name: Max Verstappen
VER.summary: Pole and victory in both the Sprint and GP; robust performance across wet and dry conditions, but only the dry GP is eligible for dry-pace weighting.

details.text: Won the Grand Prix by 7.335 seconds over Leclerc.

LEC.name: Charles Leclerc
LEC.summary: SQ P3, Sprint P3, GP qualifying P2 only 0.054s off pole, and GP P2.

details.text: A strong weekend across different conditions without a new declared persistent Singapore chassis package in LatentLap history.

ANT.name: Kimi Antonelli
ANT.summary: Continued with the new-spec package and finished on the GP podium; reports indicate he reverted to an older front wing after practice.

details.text: Do not assume he ran the new Singapore front-wing specification across all competitive sessions.

RUS.name: George Russell
RUS.summary: Quick in SQ (P2) on the Baku-spec car, crashed in the wet Sprint, qualified sixth, then recovered to P9 after a grid penalty.

details.text: The grid penalty affects the final position and should not be mistaken for a one-lap pace deficit.

PIA.name: Oscar Piastri
PIA.summary: Sprint collision with Norris in drying conditions; recovered to fifth in the dry GP.

details.text: The wet Sprint position is not representative dry race-pace evidence.

Red Bull.summary: Verstappen took both poles and both wins in Singapore; technical development and driver execution cannot be causally disentangled.

details.text: Front wing development was declared, but no isolated lap-time gain is proven.

Mercedes.summary: A deliberate split-spec test: Russell back on Baku-spec, Antonelli using the newer package.

details.text: The new front wing should be treated as tested rather than assumed raced throughout the weekend.

McLaren.summary: Wet Sprint contact and a dry GP P4/P5, amid circuit-specific brake-cooling changes.

details.text: Cooling configuration is not weighted as a persistent pace upgrade.

strategy_and_conditions.text: Sprint: rain delay, damp/wet track, intermediate tyres; excluded from future normal dry-race pace weighting.
Grand Prix: hot/humid dry race, soft-to-medium tyre stint pattern; eligible for dry-race pace weighting.
Russell penalty and Hadjar pit-lane start mean raw finishing order is not a clean one-lap ranking.
Russell reverted to Baku-spec and Antonelli remained on new Mercedes spec; preserve driver-scoped upgrade provenance.

performance_interpretation.text: Verstappen established strong pace in dry SQ, Q and Grand Prix; his wet Sprint win is a result, not direct dry pace evidence.
Mercedes component rollout differs between drivers and sessions. Avoid attributing Antonelli’s result to a new Singapore front wing without confirmation of actual race usage.

upgrades_and_technical_context.text: Singapore front-wing development was introduced for testing; Antonelli reverted to an older front wing after practice, while Russell ran Baku-spec.
upgrades_and_technical_context.reported_intent: Improve front-wake management and aero operating range.
Increase local load while keeping flow stable.

prediction_review.overall_assessment: Retrospective, pre-ingestion replay of the Singapore model state generated AFTER the event, not an independently timestamped pre-event prediction. Comparisons are useful for model diagnostics but must never be reported as genuine pre-event predictive performance. Wet Sprint race classification is confounded by conditions/incidents. Final metrics are calculated locally by finalize_r16_r17_dossiers.py.

known_exceptions.text: Singapore predictions were generated after the October 11 race, before any Singapore actual fingerprints were ingested; classify as retrospective replay, not live forecast.
Wet Sprint pace fingerprints excluded from dry-race predictor.
Hadjar Q lacked a representative lap, so Q position error is not a pure pace miss.

sprint_quali.comparison_notes: Qualifying gap errors compare seconds per lap; penalties and reliability incidents are separate context.

sprint_race.comparison_notes: Position comparison only: wet/mixed conditions and incidents confound dry-pace interpretation.

quali.comparison_notes: Qualifying gap errors compare seconds per lap; penalties and reliability incidents are separate context.

race.comparison_notes: For races, predicted per-lap gaps must not be compared with cumulative finish gaps.

knowledge_limits.text: ERS deployment and battery state cannot be directly observed from public FastF1 telemetry.
Representative race laps are not a controlled pace experiment: fuel load, tyres, traffic and temperature vary.
An upgrade declaration demonstrates intent, not an isolated measured lap-time gain.
Sprint intermediate-tyre pace cannot be treated as representative dry-race pace.
Singapore forecast was generated retrospectively after the event, even though the results had not yet been ingested; backtest statistics are not live pre-race validation.
The exact race-specification use of Antonelli’s new front wing requires caution because he reverted after practice.
